### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level interface), LocalCryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via ICryptoProvider (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fd5b536761e06a6a8f0f880211dfa8278823daf2` — the merge of head `574553aad42e888621d19a2956bc5ba8d24d13a9` into base `4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fd5b536761e06a6a8f0f880211dfa8278823daf2 && git checkout fd5b536761e06a6a8f0f880211dfa8278823daf2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 574553aad42e888621d19a2956bc5ba8d24d13a9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02 && git merge --no-ff 574553aad42e888621d19a2956bc5ba8d24d13a9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4e6dc2338acbc00eaf98bd8269317a779c6b8c02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `574553aad42e888621d19a2956bc5ba8d24d13a9`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract review of PR #21292 for card #21263, rendered 2026-10-02T02:26Z. Inputs: the card body and its three comments (triage grade, claim, dev report), the PR body and file list, the net diff of the branch against `origin/main` (merge-base confirmed, head sha equal to the one above), the check-runs on that head, ADR-0128 on `origin/main`, and the two scripts the dev's second question cites. Security family: classes, doors and positions only below; no values, no test vectors, no key labels.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`ICryptoProvider` gains one required member, `keyedDigest(plain: string)`, resolving to a string.** Accept set of the published interface narrows for implementers (every class or literal typed to it must declare the member); the caller surface widens by one method. RIGHT: this is the maintainer's option-B ruling and triage direction `5942962219` verbatim. Required rather than optional is the correct arm of that call: an optional member would be the declared-but-not-enforced property the card rejects, and it is the same reasoning ADR-0128 D1 applies to its own discriminant.
2. **The member's docblock states the three triage requirements.** (i) Keyed: the output MUST NOT be computable without the provider's key; a provider holding no key material MUST reject and never resolves to an unkeyed value, with "a MAC under an empty or publicly known key" named as a forbidden fallback. (ii) Stable per key across processes and nodes holding that key. (iii) Not a substitute for `digest`, whose contract and audit-trail stability stand. RIGHT: all three present and stated as requirements on every implementation, not as guidance.
3. **Output shape fixed in the contract: the `hmac-sha256:` prefix plus 64 lowercase hex, 76 characters.** RIGHT: it is within what a served version token can carry (the token is documented opaque; the alphabet passes an HTTP header value, a query string and a JSON string unescaped), the prefix keeps it disjoint from the unkeyed content-hash spelling, and fixing it in the contract is what lets one conformance pin judge any provider. The algorithm-named prefix is also the migration seam: a future construction takes a new prefix, never a silent change under this one.
4. **Asynchronous signature.** RIGHT: a managed-custody provider computes the MAC inside its KMS, so a synchronous signature would force the key into process; it also matches the existing `encrypt`, `decrypt` and `rotateKey` shape while `digest` stays synchronous.
5. **`digest` docblock gains one paragraph; its signature and every pre-existing sentence are byte-unchanged.** The paragraph restates the already-declared accept set (plain SHA-256 satisfies it) and cross-references the new member. RIGHT: no accept-set or behaviour change to `digest`.
6. **`LocalCryptoProvider.keyedDigest` derivation.** MAC key = HMAC-SHA-256(dataKey, label || 0x01) under a versioned label, which is RFC 5869 HKDF-Expand T(1) with the 32-byte data key as PRK (section 3.3 permits skipping Extract for a uniformly random key); the raw data key is never used as the MAC key; the derivation is deterministic, so two processes or nodes resolving one key agree. RIGHT: one key, one purpose; the output handed to callers is not keyed under the key that protects every stored secret; drift of construction is bound to a label change.
7. **Refusal without key material.** The MAC key is undefined exactly when the resolved data key is not 32 bytes, and the method then rejects with a typed error; it never falls back to an unkeyed hash or an empty-key MAC. Verified at the code: every environment and file source passes the 32-byte parser or is minted at 32 bytes, so the only route to such an instance is an explicit construction-time key, which the pin exercises with a positive control on the same route. RIGHT.
8. **No new operator secret.** The diff adds no environment variable and no key source; the one existing secret name appears only inside the refusal message. RIGHT.
9. **Pins and ablations.** Seven new cases cover the card's three (keyed versus unkeyed, equal under one key across instances and key spellings, different under a different key), plus derived-not-raw, an externally computed vector, parity across every key source, and the refusal. The three ablations described each kill the pins that own the property (unkeyed output: keyed, different-key and vector pins; refusal replaced by raw-key HMAC: the refusal pin; MAC key replaced by the data key: derived-key and vector pins). Judged by reading; the Test Core shards are the gate verdict on the suite.
10. **In-repo implementer census.** The five typed doubles gained the member. An independent search of the branch tree for the interface name, for `rotateKey` definitions and for provider wiring sites finds no further typed implementer: the two plugin-audit doubles are typed `any`, the plugin-security literal is passed `as never`, the objectql ambient-transaction literal is cast `as any`, `CryptoAdapter` and its doubles are a different interface, and the CLI, verify and service-settings sites construct the class. Gate verdict: `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and the aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` all concluded success on this head. RIGHT.
11. **Public-surface artefacts for `crypto-provider.ts`.** `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` record `ICryptoProvider (interface)` as an export; per AGENTS.md the snapshot records that an export exists, never its members, so no regeneration is owed and none is missing. `check:api-surface` runs inside the `TypeScript Type Check` job, which concluded success. RIGHT.
12. **`@objectstack/service-settings` surface.** The exported class gains one public method; the new typed error class is exported from the module but not from the package index (the index is a named export block, verified), exactly as the acceptance note states. RIGHT; the consequence for #21207's consumer is stated there (treat any rejection as serve nothing).
13. **The five doubles return deterministic stand-ins that do not imitate the keyed prefix.** RIGHT: a double should not be mistakable for real output.

### ② Semver level

- **Level `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-settings`: RIGHT.** The header of `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades "a required member on a published interface" `major` only once GA closes the launch window; until then a breaking change ships `minor` and the level is not the carrier. ADR-0087's amendment of 2026-09-13 (the level half) says the same: pre-GA, a break ships `minor`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition as the mandatory carriers. The group is pre-GA (no pre-mode file; lockstep at 17.x).
- **BREAKING banner: present**, so the ADR-0087 gate reads the changeset as declared breaking through its prose signal.
- **ADR-0087 marker: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the right category.** `runtime-interface-only` and `type-surface-only` are closed to a symbol declared under `packages/spec/src/contracts/` (the gate's predicate 2), the body carries no FROM-to-TO rewrite prescription (naming the compiler error that points at the missing member is not one), and the interface has no metadata surface for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success on this head.
- **The `Clause-②` arm, answering the dev's second question: the exact spelling for this diff is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines that reading as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; this diff widens the caller surface and narrows the set of objects that satisfy the published interface, so both facts are true and the arm is the fleet's one breaking-ness carrier that does not depend on prose (the reason #16421 added it). The `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header lists "a required member on a published interface" beside "an accept-set narrowing" as parallel examples of what grades `major` at GA; that list does not define the arm, the reader does. The absent arm reads as "no direction" by ruling (the arm is optional), breaking-ness rides on the banner today, and no gate verdict differs between the two spellings, so this is not a FAIL cause. The amendment is the seat's, not the dev's: the claim comment and PR body line 2 can carry `(narrowing)` now without moving the head; the changeset line follows on the next push to this branch if one happens, otherwise the banner carries.
- **`Clause-②: yes` holds as the level declaration:** at least one moved published package grades `minor`.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **ADR-0128 section 4 (the dev's first question) — ESCALATED: a maintainer decision, not decided here.** The trigger is met: this PR is a breaking change to `ICryptoProvider`. The ADR's text binds in two ways. First, section 4 says any one trigger "turns the deferral over" and the result is "scheduling it", so a card for D1 (required scope discriminant, delimiter-safe AAD, versioned handle, at-rest rewrap) is now owed whichever option is taken. Second, the same bullet records the preference "A queued breaking change to this interface should pull D1 in with it", and landing alone departs from a recorded preference in an accepted ADR; under Prime Directive #13 that departure is recorded on the ADR itself, which is Tier H and the maintainer's hand (option A's own dated note), or it is not taken (option B, which changes this diff and needs a new review). This record therefore does not clear that hold: the seat files `needs-user-decision` with the dev's two options as written, and the PR does not enqueue before the answer. Facts for the decision, not a recommendation: section 1.4 measures the hazard at zero instances; the population option B spares a second compile break is the out-of-repo provider set the ADR's own Consumers line names (KMS, Vault, HSM classes), which is unmeasured until landing precondition ① is on the card; option B couples a p1 security card's path to an at-rest migration project.
2. **The `Clause-②` arm (the dev's second question) — answered in ②:** `yes (narrowing)`; the seat amends; not a FAIL cause.
3. **Acceptance note: the typed refusal error is not on the package index — answered:** verified at the index; acceptable. #21207's consumer treats any rejection as "serve nothing"; exporting the class later is additive.
4. **Acceptance note and out-of-scope finding: an explicit construction-time key is not length-checked — answered:** predates the PR; both paths fail loud on first use (the cipher's own invalid-key-length error, and now the typed refusal); no public door gives a wrong answer and nothing succeeds silently, so this is not class a, b or c and no card is owed by this PR. A construction-time length check is ordinary hardening a seat may file; it is not a landing condition.
5. **Acceptance note and out-of-scope finding: `createHmac` availability on the WebContainer runtime is unmeasured — answered:** `digest` already relies on the sibling hash primitive from the same module there; if the MAC primitive were missing, the call throws, which is the permitted fail-closed direction and never a fallback. Acceptable as a note; a development sandbox, not a production door.
6. **Branch not merged with `origin/main` (now six commits behind) — answered:** none of the six touches a file in this diff or a generated spec artefact (verified by file list); CI judged the merge ref; the PR reports mergeable. Acceptable.
7. **Commit trailers written model-free — answered:** consistent with AGENTS.md; acceptable.
8. **Shared git state deepened by an additive fetch — answered:** additive only; acceptable.
9. **The narrowed-lint reading is absent from the PR body — answered:** the body amendment is the seat's; `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success, which is the gate verdict.
10. **Landing precondition ① (the out-of-repo `ICryptoProvider` census in `objectstack-ai/cloud`) is outside this review.** It stays open with the seat as the claim records; nothing here presumes that population empty.
11. **Check-runs on this head at the final read (2026-10-02T02:25Z):** all 35 concluded, none in progress; 32 success and 3 skipped by their path or opt-in filters (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`); no failure. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on in ①.9, ①.10, ①.11 and ②; nothing was run locally.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-21263-crypto-keyed-digest`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UtnxvdiN376GF3sgXwAw4d`

**VERDICT: PASS**

The verdict certifies the contract change on its merits (①), its level and declaration (②), and that every flag is answered or escalated (③). It is not a landing authorization by itself: landing still waits on the maintainer's ADR-0128 answer (③.1), on landing precondition ① (③.10), and on the gate state in ③.11.
